habitat: 해안 간척지, 사구, 삼각주, 해안 초습지

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가며, 번식지에서는 6월 하순~7월 상순에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 한반도를 지나가는 흔한 나그네새로, 해안 간척지와 사구, 삼각주, 바닷가 초습지 등에 내려앉는다. 지렁이, 새우, 조개, 곤충 같은 동물성 먹이를 주로 먹고 식물의 씨도 먹는다. 구북구 대륙 북부의 툰드라에서 이끼 덮인 땅에 접시 모양 둥지를 틀고 알 4개를 낳는다. 겨울에는 남쪽으로 내려가 남반구 남위 40도까지의 갯벌과 강어귀에서 지낸다.

art.subject: Grey Plover (Pluvialis squatarola), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean coasts in late April and May: forehead and crown whitish-grey; a broad white band starts on the forehead, runs over the eye and down the side of the neck and ends in a white patch at the side of the breast; face, throat, breast, belly and flanks solid black; vent and undertail coverts white. Upperparts spangled black and silvery-white, each feather black with white notches and tips, giving rows of white spots. Bill black, short and stout; eye large and dark; legs dark grey to blackish.
art.pose: standing on a tidal flat, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal reclaimed land with sand dunes and salt-marsh grass beside a delta, during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding (late April–May), side view standing: silver-and-black spangled upperparts, broad white band from the forehead over the eye down the neck to the breast side, solid black face and underparts, white vent, short black bill, dark grey legs
adult, in flight seen from below: black axillary patch in the armpit contrasting with the whitish underwing, white vent, barred whitish tail
juvenile (September–October), side view standing: dark brown upperparts with crisp pale spots and fringes, finely streaked breast and flanks, pale belly, short black bill
art.build: Medium-large, chunky plover, 29.5cm, clearly bigger and heavier than a Pacific Golden Plover and much larger than sand plovers. Big rounded head with a large dark eye, short thick neck, plump body. Bill black, short and stout, shorter than the head, slightly swollen at the tip. Legs medium length, dark grey. At rest the wingtips reach just past the tail tip. In flight shows a white wing bar, a white rump and a barred whitish tail, and a black patch in the 'armpit' (axillaries) on an otherwise whitish underwing. Feeds by run-stop-peck on mudflats.
avoid: Do not continue the white side stripe along the flanks to the tail; that is Pacific Golden Plover (Pluvialis fulva). Here it ends at the breast side.
Do not paint golden-yellow spangling on the upperparts (Pacific Golden Plover).
Do not paint black undertail coverts; the vent is white.
Do not paint pale armpits in flight; the black axillary patch is the key mark.
